mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 1% in both real personal income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 1% AND HOUST > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) cut of at least 0.75 percentage points within a quarter signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.75% in one quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero after such cuts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% signals a nascent recovery from a deep recession, which boosts investor optimism and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100000 AND UNRATE > 7% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
